info.title: Harbor local API
info.description: Loopback-only administration API for the Harbor local preview. Bearer sessions; JSON only.

get.description: Daemon liveness only.

Whether this Harbor still needs its first administrator, plus what the setup wizard shows. Once an administrator exists: only `needed: false` and the https hosts the console on plain http probes (decision 169).

post.description: Create the first administrator (setup code from the installer required), optionally name the machine, and get a session. Refused once an administrator exists.

get.description: A 1x1 PNG the console loads over https to learn whether this browser trusts Harbor's certificate (decision 164).
Installed version, newest release, and the state of an update in progress.

post.description: Ask GitHub Releases now whether a newer Harbor exists.
Update Harbor to the newest release: downloads, verifies, installs in place and restarts the daemon (the console reconnects).
Log in the local administrator. Rate limited. `remember` issues a 30-day session for this browser instead of the configured TTL.

get.description: Active sessions for this administrator (no token material; the current one is marked).

delete.description: Revoke every session except the current one.

post.description: The passwords of an app's Harbor logins (decision 194), for the drawer's Show. Needs the administrator password (wrong ones count against the login limits and answer 422). Turning a login on or off and setting a new password go through a configure plan (`login`).

get.description: Whether developer mode is on (packages that are not from the official catalog may then ask for the privileged and binder permissions), since when, and which installed apps hold such a permission without coming from the official catalog.

put.description: Turn developer mode on (the administrator password is required, wrong ones count against the login limits) or off (no password). Apps already installed keep running either way; with it off, installs and updates of packages that ask for privileged or binder and are not from the official catalog are refused (UNTRUSTED_SOURCE).

get.description: Daemon/Docker availability.
The app catalog: the official catalog (bundled with this release or downloaded since) plus your own uploaded or git-source packages.
The official app catalog in use (bundled with this release or downloaded since) and the last check for a newer one.

post.description: Check the catalog repository now for a newer catalog and switch to it when it downloads intact and validates. Never touches running apps; a failure leaves the catalog unchanged and is reported in `error`.

get.description: Package presentation asset (icon/gallery) from the official or uploaded package. Open (no session): static catalog content only.
Host metrics for the console (cpu, memory, disk, docker).
Volume disk usage grouped per app (docker system df, cached 60 s).
Notification history, newest first (persisting conditions are deduplicated).

delete.description: Dismiss every notification (deletes all rows; still-true persisting conditions re-create theirs on the next tick).

post.description: Mark one notification read.
Mark every notification read.

delete.description: Dismiss one notification (deletes the row; a still-true persisting condition re-creates it on the next tick).

get.description: External delivery channels (ntfy, webhook, email); secrets redacted.

put.description: Replace the delivery channels. A redacted secret ("••••") keeps the stored value.

post.description: Send a test notification to every configured channel.

get.description: Global automatic-update default for newly installed apps.

put.description: Set the global automatic-update default (opt-in; per-app toggles win).
Turn automatic updates for one app on or off.

post.description: Submit one update per app with a newer package revision (serial queue; per-app rollback).
Accept the folder at the recorded path as the new home for one storage claim (replacement drive or restored backup): stamps a fresh app-generated identity. The app must be stopped first.
Unlock one encrypted app for this boot with its encryption passphrase (or 12-word recovery key). A reboot returns it to locked.

Change an encrypted app's passphrase, or switch it between its own passphrase and Harbor's own key (next: null). current = its passphrase, its 12 words or the Harbor recovery key; omit it when this machine opens the app by itself. Returns the app's own 12 words once when they are issued.
Lock one encrypted app again (drop this boot's key; running containers keep running until stopped).

get.description: Git repositories Harbor watches as app sources.

post.description: Add a git repository as an app source: fetch the branch, import harbor/ as a package (services may build from source; provenance is the commit).
Fetch the branch head now; a newer commit becomes a new package revision.

put.description: Turn redeploy-on-commit for this source on or off.

delete.description: Forget the repository link; the imported package and installed apps stay.

get.description: All instances including retained records.
Instance detail with safe events, resource roles and setup guidance.
Home widget data proxied from the app (decision 81); null when the app declares none or the data is unusable.
Cockpit/Portainer/Tailscale/proxy state and real links.
App links (decision 126): every private link between two apps on this machine, with its network, alias and state (active, needs_provider, dormant).
Published addresses (tailnet/public) of all instances.

put.description: Change the administrator password (current password required); every other session is revoked.

post.description: Unlock this machine's key with the administrator password after a daemon restart (decision 164), so encrypted installs, restores and backups work without logging out and in. Wrong passwords count against the login limits.

get.description: The administrator login name, the Home greeting name, and whether two-factor login is on.

put.description: What Home calls you ("Good evening, Carlos"). Login name is untouched; empty clears back to the username.

post.description: Start two-factor setup: returns a fresh secret (base32) and an otpauth URL for a QR code. Not active until enabled with a live code.
Confirm the new authenticator with its current code; two-factor login is on from now.
Turn two-factor login off (password required).
Replace the Harbor recovery key: mint 12 new words (shown once), re-stamp every reachable app home, and name the ones still opening with the old card. Password required.

put.description: Name this machine (shown in Settings and on the login page); empty resets to the hostname.

get.description: Harbor's own recent log lines (systemd journal on a real host).
Redacted diagnostics bundle for bug reports (versions, host facts, instance states, disks, log tail; no secrets).
Recent container logs of one app.
Disks (mounts), removable devices, the Harbor data folder, folders in use by apps, and install locations for whole encrypted apps.
Subfolders of a host folder (system locations hidden).

post.description: Create one new folder inside a parent the Harbor service account may write to.
Mount a removable device to /mnt/<label> (root oneshot, polkit-allowed); poll GET /v1/host/storage for the result.
Unmount a removable device (refused while an app uses a folder on it).

Let Harbor manage a drive another program (a desktop automount) mounted where Harbor cannot write: unmount it, mount it the Harbor way, and stop the desktop from automounting it (decision 122). Refused while an app uses it or files are open.
Hide a drive's attention card and notification until its condition changes (decision 122).

get.description: Mount/unmount progress for one removable device.

post.description: Format a removable device as ext4 so it can hold encrypted apps (erases everything; refused while an app uses the drive). Poll GET /v1/host/devices/:name/format-status for the result.

get.description: Format progress for one removable device.

put.description: Removable-drive behaviour: auto-mount on insert, auto-start apps whose drive came back (both on by default).

get.description: Registered public domains with DNS check results, this machine's public address and which app uses each domain.

post.description: Register a domain you own and check that its DNS points at this machine.
Re-check a registered domain's DNS.

delete.description: Forget a registered domain (refused while an app is published at it).

get.description: Wallpaper state (uploaded/rotating with attribution), rotation settings (no secrets) and the launcher order.
The current wallpaper picture (open: background art loaded by /CSS, which cannot send a token).

put.description: Set your own wallpaper: a PNG, JPEG or WebP picture as a data URL (max 6 MB).

Rotating wallpapers: turn on/off, choose the source (reddit needs your own Reddit app credentials; bing and wikimedia need none), subreddits and how often. Fetches the first picture right away when turning on.

post.description: Skip to the next rotating wallpaper now.

put.description: Launcher order (instance ids, first to last). Unknown ids are dropped; missing ones keep their default position.

Customise how an app appears on the launcher: display name, icon (default, an emoji/letters on a colour, or an uploaded picture up to 1 MB) and whether Home shows it (hidden apps stay in the Store, Platform and lists).

get.description: Custom launcher icon picture of an app (open: loaded by ).

post.description: Upload a package zip. Harbor validates it like a bundled package, pins tag images by digest at the registry and writes release.json. A higher revision of an already uploaded id becomes an update for its instances.

delete.description: Remove an uploaded package (refused while an app installed from it exists).

get.description: Hostname, OS, CPU, the graphics card apps that ask for one get (decision 179), and whether Harbor may restart or shut down this machine.

post.description: Restart or shut down the machine (apps come back on their own after a restart).
Log this host into a tailnet: with an auth key, or get a login URL to approve in a browser.
Log this host out of the tailnet (withdraws tailnet addresses).

put.description: Expose the Harbor UI on the tailnet (never publicly).

delete.description: Withdraw the tailnet exposure of the Harbor UI.

get.description: The every-app Tailscale policy: on/off, whether Tailscale can publish right now (status off | waiting | on, with the reason), the apps kept off the tailnet, and where each app stands (published, pending, waiting, failed, excluded).

put.description: Turn the every-app Tailscale policy on (each app without a tailnet address gets one through its own expose plan, actor tailnet-policy, one at a time) or off (existing addresses stay; withdraw them per app). Turning it on is refused (UNSUPPORTED_CAPABILITY) while Tailscale is not ready.

The per-app switch of the every-app Tailscale policy: included false keeps this app off the tailnet (its current address, if any, stays until you withdraw it); included true lets the policy publish it again at its next check (and retries a failed attempt).
Bind an already installed tool by its loopback URL without taking ownership.

post.description: One-click install of Cockpit or Portainer from the console: starts the root oneshot (polkit-allowed); poll GET /v1/platform-tools for progress.

Create an immutable plan. Install: {kind, packageId, name?, storage?, location?, main?, links?, internet?}. Configure: {kind, instanceId, secrets?, links?, settings?, internet?}. Others: {kind, instanceId}. Operator-provided secret values never go into a plan: they travel with POST /v1/operations.

Submit an exact plan ID, or queue an action (decision 183). Requires Idempotency-Key. Plan form {planId, …}: install-location plans also need the encryption passphrase, and plans that ask for operator-provided secrets (decision 125) carry their values in `secrets` — neither is ever stored in the plan, an operation or a response. Plans that list settings with ask (decision 180: install, the settings an update adds) may carry chosen values in `settings` (not secret; SETTING_INVALID when a value is not allowed). A plan for a busy app is refused (BUSY). Action form {action: {kind, instanceId}}: a start, stop, restart, update, remove, reinstall or purge for an existing app, busy or not, joins the queue without a plan; Harbor plans it when its turn comes (an item that then needs a person stops as REVIEW_NEEDED, nothing changed). Returns 202 with the (possibly existing) operation.

acceptPermissions.description: Decision 163: true accepts the permissions the plan lists (required when it lists any).

get.description: The operation queue (decision 183): `active` = every operation not finished, in run order (the running one first, then the waiting ones; `cancellable` says which a person may cancel), `recent` = the newest finished ones (newest first, `recent` of them, default 10). List items carry no events; GET /v1/operations/:id has them and the one-time results.

post.description: Cancel a waiting operation (decision 183): only before the runner picked it (409 NOT_CANCELLABLE once it runs or has finished, and for items Harbor queued to protect something: drive-guard, link-guard, lock-guard, the backup scheduler). Nothing was done for it, so nothing is undone; a cancelled install frees its name and ports and cancels what waited for it. Returns the cancelled operation.

get.description: App homes found on mounted drives that this machine has not adopted (locked tiles; adopting prompts for the passphrase).

post.description: Adopt an app home from a drive with its encryption passphrase: unlock, wrap for silent unlock here, create the instance and start it. Ports allocate fresh on this machine. An app whose package asks for permissions (decision 163/179, listed in GET /v1/found-apps) needs acceptPermissions: true, else 409 PERMISSION_REQUIRED before anything changes.

get.description: Main-address choices available right now (decision 116): this network (HTTPS LAN, LAN or loopback), the tailnet when Tailscale has HTTPS certificates, and registered domains that point here.
LAN HTTPS state: whether https://harbor.local/ answers, the CA fingerprint to compare on the device, and the names the server cert covers.

put.description: Turn LAN HTTPS on (mints the local CA + server cert, starts the secure listeners) or off (closes them; plain HTTP stays, and HTTPS only turns off too). httpsOnly (decision 167, optional; omitted = unchanged): the plain-http console redirects to https except the CA download and the probe, and apps re-bind to loopback on their next restart so only the secure relay reaches them. Turning it on is refused unless this request itself arrived over https or from this machine.

post.description: Replace the local certificate authority with a new, name-constrained one (decision 165) and re-issue the server cert. Every device must trust the new CA again; the old CA key is deleted.

get.description: The Harbor local CA certificate (PEM). Trust it once per device, then https://harbor.local/ opens with no warning.
Backups at a glance: the global policy, place types (target packages), installed places (secrets redacted), every app with its policy and last run, what runs right now, recent runs.

put.description: Change the global backup policy: window start (local HH:MM), cadence, weekday, maximum downtime per app, retention, pause.

post.description: Install a backup place from a target package: test it, set it up (an empty place gets Harbor's backup key and your recovery key), or recognise backups of another Harbor there. The first place may issue the Harbor recovery key; it is returned once.

put.description: Rename a place or change its answers ("••••" keeps a stored secret); new answers are tested before they are saved.

post.description: Test a place again: reachable, and whether its backups open with this Harbor's key.
Clear a stale lock a crashed run left at a place (restic unlock).
Open another Harbor's backups at this place with that Harbor's recovery key (12 words). This Harbor adds its own key there, so it can restore those apps.
Uninstall a place: apps stop backing up there and its credentials are forgotten. The backups stored there are kept unless deleteBackups is true and confirmName repeats the place's name.

get.description: Apps that have restore points at this place (for restoring onto this machine).

post.description: Plan restoring an app from a place onto this machine (a new machine, or an app purged here): an install plan whose home comes from the restore point. Submit it with POST /v1/operations.

get.description: One app's backups: policy, next window, runs, restore points (refresh=true asks every place again), the copy kept by the last restore.

put.description: Turn an app's backups on or off, pick its places (fan-out) and optionally its own window/cadence (null = the global one).

post.description: Back this app up now (queued behind any app being backed up; same warm/cold passes and cap as the schedule).

delete.description: Delete the copy of the app kept aside by its last restore (root deletes it; the app is not touched).

get.description: The apps' VPN: whether this machine can run one, the tunnel (server, addresses, DNS; never a key), whether it is connected (last handshake), the every-app switch, the apps that do not go direct and the state of the host rules.

put.description: Set (or replace) the VPN from a WireGuard configuration file (wg-quick format, one [Peer], AllowedIPs covering 0.0.0.0/0; PostUp/PreUp/PostDown/PreDown/Table/FwMark/SaveConfig refused). Brings the tunnel up and reloads the rules.

delete.description: Remove the VPN. Apps that go through it keep no internet (kill switch) until one is set again or they are switched to Direct.

put.description: Send every app through the VPN (apps set to Direct go through it; offline apps stay offline).

post.description: Ask the tunnel now (last handshake, bytes) instead of the cached answer.
